title: Multiplication
description: Class 2 IMO — Multiplication as repeated addition, tables of 2, 5 and 10, equal groups and word problems for the Maths Olympiad.

topics.title: Multiplication as Repeated Addition
topics.concept:
Multiplication is a fast way to add equal groups. 3 groups of 4 = 4 + 4 + 4 = 12, which we write as 3 × 4 = 12. The sign × means times.

The order does not change the answer: 3 × 4 = 4 × 3 = 12.
recap: Order does not matter: a × b = b × a.

topics.title: Tables of 2, 5 and 10
topics.concept: The table of 2 counts in twos: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10… The table of 5 counts in fives: 5, 10, 15, 20… The table of 10 counts in tens: 10, 20, 30… Knowing these tables makes multiplication quick.

topics.title: Equal Groups & Word Problems
topics.concept: Many real situations use equal groups: rows of chairs, packets of biscuits, wheels on cars. Find how many groups and how many in each group, then multiply.

examples.problem: A car has 4 wheels. How many wheels on 3 cars?
5 packets have 2 pens each. How many pens?

recap: Look for equal groups in the problem.
Multiply groups × items in each group.

quiz.q: There are 6 boxes with 5 balls each. How many balls in all?
A hand has 5 fingers. How many fingers on 2 hands?

questions.q: Which is the odd one out (three equal 12):  3 × 4, 2 × 6, 6 × 2, 5 × 3?
A tricycle has 3 wheels. How many wheels on 4 tricycles?
Each student gets 2 notebooks. How many notebooks for 8 students?
Sweets come in packs of 10. How many sweets in 4 packs?
There are 5 rows of chairs with 5 chairs in each row. How many chairs in all?
A box holds 2 rows of 5 chocolates. How many chocolates in 2 such boxes?
